goal: Propose a project-wide error handling strategy (results vs errors vs defects) to end recurring disputes seen in several open PRs.
Written as a discussion-starting design document, not a finished policy.
reviewability: Ready to review as a discussion document, but the text is disputed and the author is actively incorporating feedback.
Expect substantial rewrites before any version could be merged.
agreement: Disputed: concept ACKs from several members (sedited, josibake, willcl-ark) welcome having a strategy doc, but strongly object to this specific proposal's exceptions-first approach.
Concept NACK from ajtowns who says the doc contradicts existing practice (util::Expected, util::Result) and would introduce technical debt.
Approach NACK from l0rinc who argues for return-value/functional style instead of exceptions.
Substantive unresolved objections from maflcko and mzumsande about defect handling varying by subsystem (p2p, RPC) and about doc placement.
Author (purpleKarrot) engaging with all objections but hasn't yet revised the text to address them.

result.summary: This PR adds a new developer-facing design document, doc/error-handling.md, proposing a single project-wide error handling strategy for Bitcoin Core: results (return values) for successful outcomes including domain-negative outcomes, exceptions for errors outside program correctness, and fail-fast defects for internal invariant violations. It explicitly says new code must not introduce std::expected/util::Result-style return-value error propagation, and instead directs the whole codebase toward exceptions. The author frames it as a discussion-starting design doc reacting to unresolved error-handling disagreements visible in three other open/merged PRs.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core currently lacks an agreed error-handling strategy, causing repeated, unresolved bikeshedding across unrelated PRs (validation DB error handling, P2P block I/O error handling, coins/dbwrapper fatal errors) about whether to use exceptions, util::Expected/Result, or ad hoc mechanisms. This is felt by contributors and reviewers of those PRs, who currently re-litigate the question each time.

open_concerns: ajtowns: doc contradicts existing codebase practice (util::expected.h, util::result.h) and merging it would create technical debt to migrate away from those; also disagrees exceptions are better in general.
l0rinc: approach NACK, argues for functional/return-value style over exceptions, calls exceptions 'unpredictable side-effects' and 'surprises'; extensive back-and-forth with author, no resolution.

mzumsande: a single project-wide defect-handling policy is wrong given how differently subsystems (validation vs p2p vs RPC) already handle defects (Assume/CHECK_NONFATAL vs abort); prefers doc describing multiple domain-specific solutions rather than one global policy. Author responded 2026-09-03 asking if clarifying wording resolves this; no reply yet.

maflcko: doc is in the wrong location (should be doc/developer-notes.md, not a new file) and would create internally contradictory documentation with existing docs (util/check.h, result.h, expected.h) unless those are updated too; also worries about review overhead from broader exception use across threads.
sedited: raised open technical questions (bad_alloc classification, serialization error handling, checked/unchecked exception taxonomy) not yet fully answered.

willcl-ark: asked why exceptions were chosen over LLVM-style Expected/Error, and flagged that adopting this would require auditing exception safety/thread boundaries broadly; author answered but willcl-ark has not confirmed satisfaction.
resolved_concerns: Personal-attack tone flagged by josibake/willcl-ark was addressed by participants moderating their language going forward.
discussion.author_status: active, said (2026-09-03) intends to incorporate mzumsande's and others' feedback before revising, but no revision pushed yet

reviewability.label: Author reworking
reviewability.reason: The author stated on 2026-09-03 they will incorporate feedback (from mzumsande and others) before revising the document, meaning the current text is known to be superseded by an upcoming rewrite. Reviewing the current wording in depth is likely to be partially wasted effort until that revision lands, though the core concept can still be evaluated now.

agreement.summary: Concept ACKs for having a strategy doc, but concept/approach NACKs on this specific exceptions-first proposal from ajtowns and l0rinc, plus substantive unresolved concerns from mzumsande and maflcko.
agreement.reason: Multiple members welcome establishing an error-handling strategy in principle (sedited, josibake, willcl-ark concept ACK), but the specific direction (mandating exceptions, banning util::Expected/Result) is contested by ajtowns (concept NACK, contradicts existing codebase direction) and l0rinc (approach NACK, prefers functional/return-value style). mzumsande argues a single global policy is wrong given subsystem differences; author asked for confirmation this is resolved but no reply yet. maflcko says the doc cannot merge as-is and flags a wrong location plus contradictions with existing docs.
evidence: ajtowns: 'NACK, this isn't a problem that needs a 750 word essay... the essay provided doesn't reflect existing practice (eg util/expected.h or util/result.h)'
l0rinc: 'Approach NACK, instead of presenting your personal opinion as the only way forward, try gathering info first on the project's needs'

mzumsande: 'I see no reason why we would regress on these pragmatic, domain-specific solutions in favor of a global policy from the drawing board.' — author asked 2026-09-03 if clarifying wording resolves this, no reply yet
maflcko: 'it can absolutely not be merged in its current form, while ignoring the review feedback above... doc/error-handling.md is the wrong place to put the docs'
sedited, josibake, willcl-ark: concept ACK for having a strategy document in general

enables: Could inform resolution of ongoing disputes in #34931 (merged), #35003 (open), #34132 (open) about error handling in validation/DB/P2P code, if consensus on a strategy is reached

categories.name: docs
categories.evidence: The PR's sole content is a new design document under doc/, matching the docs category's design-document scope, and carries the Docs label.
categories.rationale: P2 because this is a design document intended to resolve a real, recurring disagreement across multiple validation/mempool-adjacent PRs (#34931 merged, #35003 open, #34132 open) about how errors should be handled, and the category file counts a design doc that unblocks a project as leverage. However the PR is far from settled: several senior members (ajtowns, l0rinc, mzumsande, maflcko) substantively disagree with both the direction and even the placement of the document, so its value depends entirely on reaching consensus, which has not happened. It is not P1 because no user or security harm currently exists from the doc's absence, and it is not lower than P2 because the underlying disagreement it targets is real and has already caused friction in several other PRs.

uncertainties: Whether this design doc will ultimately be merged in anything resembling its current form, given strong disagreement on the core exceptions-vs-return-value question.
Whether the category rubric's 'design doc that unblocks a project' framing applies here given the strategy itself, not just its documentation, is contested.
How to weigh the mix of concept ACKs (for having a doc) against concept/approach NACKs (for this doc's content) in the agreement assessment.
result.card: This PR adds doc/error-handling.md, a new design document proposing that Bitcoin Core adopt exceptions for error propagation, return values only for genuine domain results, and fail-fast defects for programming bugs, explicitly banning new util::Expected/util::Result-style APIs. The author (purpleKarrot, a maintainer) opened it to settle recurring disagreements visible in three other PRs (#34931, #35003, #34132) about how errors should be handled in validation and DB code. Discussion is heavy and substantive: several members concept-ACK having a strategy doc at all (sedited, josibake, willcl-ark) but ajtowns concept-NACKs and l0rinc approach-NACKs the specific exceptions-first direction, arguing it contradicts existing codebase practice (util::Expected/Result) and would create technical debt. mzumsande and maflcko separately argue a single global policy is wrong given how differently subsystems like p2p and RPC already handle defects, and maflcko says the doc is in the wrong location and cannot merge as-is. The author is actively engaging and said on 2026-09-03 they plan to revise the document to address feedback, so the current text should be treated as a moving target.
